sections.title: Level 3 Advanced Strategy
sections.content: In Sentence Improvement Level 3, attention must be given to deep sentence structure, clause relationships, and precision of meaning. Follow 4–5 steps: Step 1: Identify the main clause and subordinate clause. Step 2: Recognize special structures such as Inversion, Subjunctive mood, and Perfect tenses. Step 3: Check the logical relationship between modifiers and the subject. Step 4: Remove unnecessary words or redundancy. Step 5: Choose the best option based on fluency and clarity of meaning.

sections.title: Inversion (No sooner, Hardly, Not only)
sections.content: Step 1: Check whether the sentence begins with 'No sooner', 'Hardly', 'Scarcely', or 'Not only'. Step 2: In such cases, the auxiliary verb appears before the subject. Step 3: Use the correct pair (No sooner... than, Hardly... when). Step 4: Ensure correct verb tense agreement. Example: 'No sooner he arrived than it started raining' is incorrect. Correct: 'No sooner had he arrived than it started raining.'

sections.title: Correct Use of the Subjunctive Mood
sections.content: Step 1: Identify expressions such as 'It is important that', 'It is essential that', 'It is crucial that'. Step 2: Use the base form of the verb in the that-clause. Step 3: Do not add s/es to the verb even if the subject is singular. Step 4: Maintain the formal tone of the sentence. Example: 'It is crucial that he studies hard' is incorrect. Correct: 'It is crucial that he study hard.'

sections.title: Removing Redundancy
sections.content: Step 1: Identify words whose meaning is already implied. Step 2: Remove repetitive or unnecessary words. Step 3: Make the sentence concise. Step 4: Keep only essential words. Example: 'Revert back to me' is incorrect because 'revert' already means 'back'. Correct: 'Revert to me.'

sections.title: Dangling Modifier Correction (Participles and Gerunds)
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the ing phrase or participle phrase. Step 2: Check which subject it modifies. Step 3: Ensure that the subject performing the action follows the phrase. Step 4: If the subject is incorrect, restructure the sentence. Example: 'Walking through the park, the flowers looked beautiful' is incorrect. Correct: 'Walking through the park, I saw beautiful flowers.'

sections.title: Complex Perfect Tense (Have had, Had had)
sections.content: Step 1: Identify auxiliary verbs (have, had). Step 2: Determine whether the tense is present perfect, past perfect, or past perfect continuous. Step 3: Match the tense according to context. Step 4: Understand the sequence of events. Example: 'He had had lunch before the meeting started' is correct because the lunch occurred earlier.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Forgetting the auxiliary verb in inversion structures. 2. Adding s/es to verbs in the subjunctive mood. 3. Using unnecessary or redundant words. 4. Changing meaning due to dangling modifiers. 5. Incorrect sequence in perfect tenses.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 3, focus on sentence structure, clause sequence, and grammatical precision. Place the auxiliary before the subject in inversion, use the base verb in the subjunctive mood, remove redundancy, link modifiers with the correct subject, and understand the order of events in complex perfect tenses.

tricks.title: No Sooner Rule
tricks.explanation: After 'No sooner', use auxiliary + subject and the word 'than'.
tricks.example: No sooner had he arrived than the train left.

tricks.title: Hardly/Scarcely Pair
tricks.explanation: Hardly or Scarcely is followed by 'when' and uses inversion.
tricks.example: Hardly had she entered when the phone rang.

tricks.title: Not Only Structure
tricks.explanation: After 'Not only', the auxiliary verb comes before the subject and the structure must remain balanced.
tricks.example: Not only did he finish the work but he also helped others.

tricks.title: Subjunctive Base Verb Rule
tricks.explanation: After expressions like important, essential, or crucial, use the base form of the verb.
tricks.example: It is essential that she attend the meeting.

tricks.title: Redundancy Removal Trick
tricks.explanation: Remove words whose meaning is already included.

tricks.title: Dangling Modifier Check
tricks.explanation: The subject following the phrase must be the one performing the action.
tricks.example: Having completed the task, she went home.

tricks.title: Have Had Pattern
tricks.explanation: In present perfect, 'have had' is used for ownership or experience.
tricks.example: I have had this car for five years.

tricks.title: Had Had Sequence
tricks.explanation: In past perfect, 'had had' shows an earlier event in the past.
tricks.example: He had had dinner before they arrived.

tricks.title: Event Order Shortcut
tricks.explanation: When two events happened in the past, the earlier one takes past perfect tense.
tricks.example: She had left before I reached.
